intended_object: The affine coordinate function X_j/X_i (for j ≠ i) on the standard affine chart D₊(X_i) of projective space. It is an element of the degree-zero homogeneous localization R[X_k]_(X_i). This is inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
`Away.mk 𝒜 hf n x hx` is the degree-zero fraction x / f^n, where `hf` says f is homogeneous (here of degree 1, since f = X_i) and x has degree n · deg f. The definition takes n = 1 and x = X_j, which is homogeneous of degree 1, so it gives exactly X_j / X_i in `Away 𝒜 (X i)`. The companion lemma `coordinateRatio_val` confirms this: the underlying value is `Localization.mk (X j) ⟨X i ^ 1, _⟩`.

The generality is the natural one. The base ring R is an arbitrary commutative ring, and the index type ι is arbitrary; it need not be finite.

Mathlib has no named declaration for this specific coordinate. The general constructor it uses is `HomogeneousLocalization.Away.mk`.
